chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who consumes the wealth of his brother unjustly and does not return it to him, will eat an ember of Fire on the Day of Resurrection.'

key_terms.جَذْوَةً: an ember / a piece of wood from fire

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of unjustly consuming another's wealth according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to underscore the severity of *akl al-mal bi'l-batil* (consuming wealth unjustly), a key theme in Shia jurisprudence regarding economic rights. The metaphor of consuming an 'ember of Fire' vividly illustrates that the injustice is not merely a financial debt but a spiritual consumption that directly impacts one's standing in the Hereafter, linking material greed to eternal punishment.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washha, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying, ‘The one who consumes the wealth of his brother unjustly and does not return it to him would eat an ember of Fire on the Day of Judgement’.
en.sarwar: 15. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from al- Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from Ali ibn abu Hamza from abu Basir who has said the following: “
I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘Whoever consumes the property of his brother (in belief) unjustly and does not return it to him, he will have to eat a chunk of fire on the Day of Judgment.’”
